reasoning: The two sets are close. A wins narrowly, on RL depth and test precision. Each of A's environments is a ladder of RL ideas. Snake goes from a lookup-table learner to a neural value learner (DQN) to a small image network (CNN), with ablations that remove one piece at a time. The fish tank compares plain policy gradient (REINFORCE) against clipped policy gradient (PPO). Predator-prey goes from fixed opponents to naive co-learning to an opponent pool, with cross-play tables. The physics are exact, and A keeps game-over and time-limit endings separate so learning targets bootstrap correctly. A's golden test cases (TC) give exact expected values: Snake boards, ball reflection, returns-to-go, advantage estimates (GAE), the clipped objective. A's task packets carry every frozen type a builder needs. A's weaknesses: one big milestone per stage (M1 has 31 tasks and bundles the CNN, ablations, library reference and replay); pipeline step tables that list every environment and agent constructor for all three stages, with full behaviour rather than a minimal spine; a brief still framed around Snake only ('Not doing: Designing future environments now') even though the spec fully defines all three; and public contract helpers kept only so tests can reach them. B reads more easily and its pipelines are cleaner, with real baseline spines: online Q-learning before the replay buffer and target network are added, and REINFORCE as PPO's first version. B also adds hand-solved check worlds before training. Its fish-tank split (one fish → many → local sight) follows dependency lines. But B's M1 leaves out the replay viewer, a core success criterion, and M2 is a carved-off bundle of DQN tuning, replay, video, reference check and write-up. One M1 test case (TC-17) has an open re-derive item, and the M1-T09 spine packet leaves out WorldSpec/TeamSpec/Step/Policy, which the training loop needs. B's tests are mostly property checks rather than exact expected values, and its environments teach less (no lookup-table rung, no ablations, no naive-vs-pool comparison).
